deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the final page of the draft of Riemann's paper 'Zwei allgemeine Sätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten' (dated 1857 and published posthumously in the Werke, 1876). The previous page sets up the problem as follows. One has a system y = (y_1,...,y_n) of multivalued functions of x. Its branch points are a, b, ..., g, and its monodromy substitutions are constant matrices (A), (B), ..., (G). Exponents (local behaviour) are prescribed. By raising exponents, a system is reached that is determined up to a common constant factor. That factor is fixed by normalising the leading coefficient of the first component of (A)^{-1}(y) at x=a to 1. Studying how this normalised system changes when a branch point, e.g. a, moves gives the theorem: y is, as a function of a, again a system of the same type. Its branch points are b, ..., g, x, and its substitutions are composed of (A), ..., (G). There is an exceptional case: the free constants may not suffice to keep all substitutions constant while a moves. Then the system is regarded as a degenerate case of a system with lower exponents, in which certain initial coefficients of the local series for (A)^{-1}(y), ..., vanish for those special positions of a, ..., g. This page opens with that last clause.

Main statement of the page, in modern terms. Let t = (a, b, ..., g) be the p-1 branch points and x the variable, so there are p variables (t, x) in total. The normalised solution vector Y(x; t) is then a multivalued function on the complement of the hyperplanes {x = t_i}, {t_i = t_j} in C^p. Analytic continuation along any closed loop in that space returns Y either to itself or to M·Y, where M is a constant matrix. M is generated by the monodromy matrices (A), ..., (F). Only p-2 of these are arbitrary: there are p-1 branch-point matrices, and the last, (G), is fixed by the product relation (A)(B)...(G) = 1. In modern language this is isomonodromic deformation. With the monodromy representation held fixed while the poles move, the solution extends to a multivalued function of all positions, with monodromy (of the braid/pure-braid group action) expressible through the original generators.

Riemann then declines to go further: neither these functions of several variables nor the integration methods the theorem gives for linear ODEs are pursued here. He adds two remarks.
(i) An integral of an algebraic function is a special case. My filling: w = ∫ f(x) dx with f algebraic satisfies a linear ODE such as w'' - (f'/f) w' = 0. Its monodromy on the pair (w, 1) is unipotent, of the form [[1, ω],[0, 1]] with ω a period.
(ii) Applying the principle to such integrals, now viewed as functions of x and the branch points, leads to the functions represented by general theta series with arbitrary period moduli. This points to the Jacobi inversion problem and Riemann theta functions, with moduli depending on branch points.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.
The count 'p-2 beliebig gegebenen Systemen' is correct with p variables: p-1 branch points plus x, one product relation among p-1 monodromies.
The main claim is not proved here; it rests on the sketched argument of the previous page.

The exceptional case, where free constants are insufficient, is treated only heuristically by appeal to lower exponents. Rigorous treatment came later via Schlesinger's equations and Riemann–Hilbert theory (Plemelj, Bolibruch's counterexamples showing subtleties).

results.what: Normalised solutions of a Fuchsian system with fixed monodromy, viewed as functions of the branch points and x, form a multivalued function of p variables whose monodromy is a linear substitution composed of the given (A),...,(F)
results.modern_name: Isomonodromic (monodromy-preserving) deformation; monodromy of the deformation over configuration space
results.usually_credited_to: R. Fuchs (1905, Painlevé VI), L. Schlesinger (1905/1912, Schlesinger equations); later Jimbo–Miwa–Ueno (1980s)

results.what: Abelian integral of an algebraic function regarded as a special case of such functions (solution of a linear ODE with unipotent monodromy)
results.modern_name: Abelian integrals as solutions of Picard–Fuchs-type linear ODEs

results.what: Applying the deformation principle to such integrals leads to general theta series with arbitrary period moduli
results.modern_name: Riemann theta functions with moduli depending on branch points (Thomae-type dependence, period matrices as functions of branch points)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the closing passage of Riemann's 1857 'Zwei allgemeine Sätze' fragment, published in his Werke (1876). Historians already credit Riemann with anticipating isomonodromic deformation here, so nothing is new.
